newsitem.title: INDIA: Former Gandhi aide has second thoughts on auction.
newsitem.headline: Former Gandhi aide has second thoughts on auction.

text.p: Mahatma Gandhi's former secretary said on Thursday he had asked a London-based auction house to postpone the sale of a collection of writings by the Indian nationalist leader after a government appeal.

Venkataraman Kalyanam told Reuters in the southern city of Madras that the Indian government had asked him to cancel the sale of documents, which he said could fetch up to one million stg ($1.6 million).

Kalyanam said the government had argued that the sale would put the papers, including many speeches Gandhi made in the six months before he was assassinated in 1948, in the hands of speculators and deprive scholars of access.
Auction house Phillips said on Monday the writings, which were stashed in Kalyanam's cupboard in Madras for nearly 50 years, would be sold in London.

"I have sent...a fax message asking them to withhold the sale which was scheduled for this November," said Kalyanam, who gave up a government job to become Gandhi's private secretary in 1945. "But I have yet to get a reply from them," he added.
Many of the 450 handwritten papers were scrawled on the backs of envelopes or old letters by the environment-conscious apostle of non-violence.

"Gandhiji then was a very disillusioned man, unhappy with the way India was veering away from his path of truth, non-violence, communal harmony and austerity," Kalyanam said. "He made no bones about his dismay."
There are also letters written to Britain's wartime prime minister, Winston Churchill, and to Louis Mountbatten, the last British viceroy of India before independence in 1947.
Kalyanam kept the writings in his home and had decided to sell them to raise money for a Hawaii-based Hindu charity, which wants to build a new temple.

The 75-year-old former civil servant said the Indian government told him an auction would put priceless archives in the hands of monied speculators and that the government did not have the resources to compete in bidding. He declined to disclose who in the government had pressed him.
